module.takeover_extended.checks: Tests the names brought by the complementary sources and by brute-force (alias to an abandoned third-party service) with the engine of the "Subdomain takeover" module, and installs the still-valid service fingerprints from older versions (about thirty more services).
module.takeover_extended.fix:
These names come from the additional sources or from brute force, and are often missing from your inventory: for each name flagged, first delete the dangling DNS record (CNAME, or A/AAAA), at your DNS host or registrar.
If it must stay in service: recreate the expected resource at the third-party provider from YOUR account, with exactly the name the CNAME points to, and attach the custom domain to it; enable domain ownership verification when the provider offers it (TXT record).
"To check" finding: open the name in a browser. A "site not found" page from the provider or a missing resource is handled as a possible takeover, even if the provider requires proof of ownership: delete the record to be safe.
List all CNAME records of the zone (zone export) and check that each target still exists and belongs to you; delete those whose target is gone, including on forgotten names that appear in no certificate log.
Remember the order: before terminating a third-party service (site, hosting, bucket, free trial), delete its DNS record, never the other way round.
If the subdomain may have been taken over: consider it compromised, check the certificates issued for that name, invalidate sessions and cookies carried by the parent domain, and check that no service (OAuth redirects, CORS, CSP, SPF) still trusts that name.
Check with `dig +short CNAME subdomain.example.com` (no answer left after deletion), then run the scan again.
module.takeover_extended.fix_snippet:
# Bash
dig +short CNAME app.example.com
dig app-old.example.net | grep "status:"
curl -sI --max-time 10 https://app.example.com

# PowerShell
Resolve-DnsName app.example.com -Type CNAME
Resolve-DnsName app-old.example.net
module.takeover_extended.title: Subdomain takeover (extended names)
module.takeover_extended.why: A hijacked subdomain serves the attacker's content under the victim's name. Forgotten names, absent from certificate logs, are precisely the ones whose alias dangles toward a cancelled service.
takeover_extended.score_confirmed: {count} possible subdomain takeover(s) among the extended names
takeover_extended.score_none: No takeover among the extended names tested
